chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Abu Ja'far, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from al-Masharqi, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who deliberately broke his fast for days in the month of Ramadan, what is upon him regarding the expiation? He wrote: Whoever breaks his fast for one day in the month of Ramadan, upon him is freeing a believing slave, and he must fast one day in place of that day.

key_terms.كَفَّارَة: Expiation or compensation for a religious violation
key_terms.يَوْمًا بَدَلَ يَوْمٍ: One day in place of one day

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for deliberately breaking a fast in Ramadan?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS) recorded in al-Isfahar, the specific expiation for deliberately breaking a fast is defined as freeing a believing slave and fasting one day in compensation. This ruling reflects the early juristic view within the Shia tradition, distinguishing it from the more commonly cited three-month fast found in Sunni sources, and highlights the practical application of kaffarah in the context of the Prophet's time.
